2.2 National Disaster Relief Fund 
 
Recommendation 
 
2.2.1 The Committee understands that vagaries of nature cannot be controlled through policy but 
sound policy can be evolved so that loss of lives, livestock and property can be minimized by taking 
timely steps to remain prepared for the disaster. However by taking adequate repair/compensation 
measures rehabilitation of the victims can also be done. The Committee notes that rehabilitation and 
infrastructure restoration, etc., has to be done by the concerned departments of the Central 
Government and the State Governments which creates compartmentalization of reaction to the 
disasters. Therefore the Committee recommends  that the MHA needs to strengthen its role to

natural disasters. In order to strengthen the existing disaster management system, the Disaster 
Management Act, 2005 was enacted and notified on December 26, 2005. The Act provides for 
institutional mechanisms for drawing up and monitoring the implementation of the disaster 
management plans, which includes holistic, coordinated, and prompt response to any calamity 
situation in the country and ensures measures by various wings of government for prevention, 
coordination, mitigation and for minimizing the effects of calamities. Strengthening of the disaster 
management mechanism is a continuing process and efforts are continuously being made.

infrastructural requirements of Police as elaborated above by the Ministry particularly the ongoing

3.1 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) 
 
Recommendation 
 
3.1.1 The Committee observes that there is always a disparity between the assessment of damage due 
to disaster made by the States and the assessment made by the Ministry of Home Affairs. The reason 
for the same could be that the Central study teams are sent for an assessment of damages and 
casualties months after the occurrence of disaster and by the time that teams reaches the disaster-
affected area, the signs of disaster are on the verge of diminishing. Therefore, the Committee 
recommends that the Study Teams should make a preliminary visit to the disaster affected areas, within 
a week of the disaster for quick and initial assessment of the damage. Further, if preliminary damage 
assessment is done jointly with the concerned State Governments then chances of differences in 
assessment of damage is likely to be minimized. 
(Para 3.4.8 of 224th Report) 
Action Taken 
 
3.1.2 The concerns of the Committee have been noted. The Central Government had taken a 
significant decision on 19/08/2019 for constitution of Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) 
immediately in the aftermath of any natural calamity of severe nature and even before the receipt of 
Memorandum from the State Government. Accordingly, in consultation with the State Government, the 
IMCT along with the concerned officers of State Government, visits the affected areas to have the first 
hand assessment of the damages caused and the relief work carried out by the State Administration. 
 
3.1.3 It may also be noted that State Government in their Memorandum generally projects their 
requirements over and above or on other than approved items / norms, which are outside the purview of 
SDRF / NDRF norms, such as restoration works of long term / permanent nature and ineligible items, 
etc. These factors attribute the huge difference / gap in demand of the State and actual approval from 
the GOI. Therefore, the State Government should prepare Memorandum in conformity with approved 
items and norms of assistance. Therefore, all the States have been advised from time to time that while 
submitting Memorandum for assistance from NDRF, they should prepare it strictly as per the norms 
only. 
 
Further Recommendation 
 
3.1.4 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and observes that no firm commitment has 
been given with regard to visit of the Central Study team within a week's time for assessment of 
damage caused by disaster. Therefore, the Committee reiterates its recommendation that the 
Study Teams should make a preliminary visit to the disaster affected areas within a week of the 
disaster for quick and initial assessment of the damage so that the funds can be released in time 
on the basis of realistic assessment. 
 
 
 
 

 
 
27 
 
Recommendation 
 
3.1.5 The Committee takes note of the above measures and feels the need to prepare and engage 
communities to deal with all phases of a Disaster: preparedness, prevention, mitigation, response, and 
recovery. To build disaster resilient communities, the communities need to be empowered first so that 
it can cope with the adverse effects of natural hazards. This is the most sustainable approach in dealing 
with disaster risks. The Committee strongly recommends that in the pattern of National Cadet Corps 
(NCC), a Disaster Management Training Corps (DMTC) can be initiated in schools and colleges not 
only to play the role of a strong civilian corps to support the Disaster Management Teams but also to 
disseminate the practices in disaster management at the community level. 
(Para 3.4.13 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
3.1.6 National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) initiated a pilot scheme – Aapda Mitra 
with a view to create a pool of volunteers by training of 200 volunteers in each 30 project districts of 
25 States of India in disaster response so that they can respond to their community's immediate needs 
in the aftermath of a disaster thereby enabling them to undertake basic relief and rescue tasks during 
emergency situations such as floods, flash-floods, urban flooding. These volunteers are selected from 
the community including Students residing in flood prone districts. Preference is given to Ex-
Servicemen, Civil Defence, Home Guards and Community Services. 5116 volunteers have been trained 
so far. Assam, Bihar, Kerala, Maharashtra, Odisha, Tripura, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh are also 
using their services in COVID-19 response. 
 
3.1.7 It is also informed that based on the recommendations of States/UTs to upscale it in multi-
hazard districts and to train more volunteers, NDMA is planning to upscale it in 350 districts prone to 
landslide, earthquake, cyclone and floods with a view to train 100000 volunteers in India in the 
current financial year. 
 
3.1.8 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) is conducting Community Awareness Programmes 
(CAP), School Safety Programmes (SSP), Mock Exercises as a part of Capacity Building programmes

3.4.4 The Committee notes the submission of MHA on the upcoming Census and NPR. The 
Committee is not quite convinced with the reply of the Ministry that the Aadhaar is an individual data 
and in order to create a family database, NPR exercise has been undertaken.The Committee is of the 
opinion that the Aadhaar is not just an individual’s data but it is also tied up with ration card, pan card, 
etc. Aadhaar metadata also includes entire family’s surname, address, etc. Therefore, the Committee 
fails to understand as to why this should be treated as individual data only. In view of the same, the 
Committee would like the MHA to explore the feasibility of using the Aadhaar metadata for the 
Census and updation of NPR in 2020-21. Further, the Committee recommends that all the States/UTs 
should be fully convinced on various issues pertaining to the NPR which commences in April to have 

 
 
31 
 
a national consensus so that there is absolute clarity and no apprehension among remaining people 
across the country which will help in conducting these exercises in a smooth manner. 
(Para 3.9.13 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
3.4.5 Aadhaar is individual data. In Aadhaar database consolidated details of a family is not 
available nor from this database can a family structure be created without visiting each household and 
collecting information such as relationship among family members. However, NPR database is 
created by collecting family-wise data and it can be strengthened by linking Aadhaar to each member. 
Various welfare schemes of State and Central Governments are generally family based for which NPR 
data may be used. 
 
3.4.6 Aadhaar provides a unique identity number to individuals. Aadhaar database contains bare 
minimum demographic parameters of an individual while NPR database is a comprehensive family 
database which can be further enriched by linking with Aadhaar number to provide a base frame of 
population for preparing various public welfare schemes. During updation of NPR 2020, the Aadhaar 
number is being collected on voluntary basis. Presence of Aadhaar number in the NPR database will 
facilitate its integration with other databases and will also help in cleaning of various databases. NPR 
database may be shared with Central and State Governments to prepare Public Welfare oriented 
schemes. 
 
3.4.7 This office is in constant touch with State / UT Governments on various issues related to 
conduct of Census 2021 and updation of NPR. However, in view of outbreak of COVID-19 pandemic, 
the Phase I of Census 2021 and updation of NPR, which as to begin on various dates decided by the

4.2 Delhi Police 
 
Recommendation 
 
4.2.1 The Committee reiterates its following recommendations made in its 222nd Report on The 
management of Worsening Traffic Situation in Delhi: 
 
(i) with the increasing population and increasing number of vehicles in Delhi, it has 
become very difficult to regulate the flow of traffic manually and therefore, the Committee 
strongly supports incorporation of Intelligent Traffic Management systems (ITMS) for better 
management of traffic (Para 4.6.6). 
(ii) The Committee observes that the computer-based Area Traffic Control System is 
operational in many Southeast Asian countries for the last three decades but is anguished to 
learn that Delhi, the capital of India, does not have any computer-based system for managing 
the traffic on the Roads. For example in the Philippines, for traffic management, a computer-
based induction and sensor-based intersection system were installed around 30 years ago. 
(Para 4.6.7). 
(iii) The Committee feels that although ITMS projects have finally been envisaged for 
Delhi, the Committee is deeply concerned at the very slow pace of progress being made in 
devising the project and taking up just the pilot project. (Para 4.6.8).

Action Taken 
 
4.2.2 Delhi Traffic Police has informed that the pilot ITMS has been initiated and under this project 
Red Light Violation Detection (RLVD) cameras at 34 important intersections have been installed in 
Delhi based on State-of-the-art 3D Radar technology. Similarly, Over Speed Violation Detection 
(OSVD) camera system has also been installed at 100 locations all over the city. These systems are 
computer based and controlled from the Traffic Command  Centre established at Traffic Police 
Headquarters, Todapur. Traffic violations such as violation of traffic signal, stop line, over-speeding, 
driving against the flow of traffic, etc. are detected by intelligent sensors and notices are sent to the 
violators through SMS. The violators have been provided facility of online payment through SBI e-
pay gateway. The entire system is automated based on latest technology. The system is working 
satisfactorily and Delhi Traffic Police is considering expanding it at other strategic locations. The 
project of Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) planned to be implemented in a phased 
manner: - Preparation and approval of detailed project report (DPR) by September  2020  (16  weeks

stagnation and other issues. The Committee reiterates its recommendation made at para 4.3.19 
of the 224th  Report of the DFG (2020-21) of MHA  and urges the Ministry to furnish their views 
on said recommendation. 
(Para 3.6.7) 
National Intelligence Grid (NATGRID) 
 
 The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Ministry that budgetary projections 
of Rs. 294.04 was made for BE 2020-21 as NATGRID Solutions are to go live by December, 2020 
and accordingly, all IT equipment of NATSTAR and OSINT and Solution development are 
planned to be undertaken in 2020-21. Therefore, the Committee recommends the Ministry to 
expedite the process of procurement of all IT equipments of NATSTAR and OSINT and solution 
development so as to achieve early operationalisation of NATGRID that is a integrated 
intelligence master database for counter-terrorism operations. 
(Para 3.7.5) 

 
 
67 
 
Modernization of Police Forces 
 
 The Committee notes the shortfall of funds for Modernisation of Police Forces Scheme 
and feels that the modernization of Police Forces through the induction of new equipments, 
training and technological up-gradation of capabilities is also equally important. Police Forces 
should be sufficiently equipped to meet the entire spectrum of security challenges. Therefore, the 
Committee, recommends that more budget may be requested at RE stage.  Further, a major 
share of the modernization budget is spent on improving the infrastructure of the police forces 
but training State Police Forces in relation to its behavior with public is essential to improve its 
image as modern day police forces. The Committee further recommends that it should be 
mandatory for the State police forces to spend the allocated budget for giving better training to 
all police personnel.  
(Para 3.8.3) 
 
Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS) 
 
 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry that all the States have launched their 
Citizens Portal under the CCTNS and 4.85 crore citizens request have been received so far till 
29th February, 2020. The Committee would like to be apprised about the action taken/ disposal 
of the requests made under CCTNS. The Committee also notes the reply that online filing of e-
FIR has been launched by three States/ UTs, namely Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan for 
property and vehicle thefts in cases where accused are unknown. The Committee recommends 
that online filing of e-FIR should be expanded to all States/UTS and devise a mechanism to 
register e-FIRs for different category of complaints. 
(Para 3.9.5) 
 
Security Related Expenditure (SRE) and Special Infrastructure Scheme for LWE areas 
 
 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry that Rs. 1687 crore has been released since 
2014-15 under the Security Related Expenditure (SRE) scheme and urge the Ministry to furnish 
data on the utilization of the funds since 2014-15. The Committee also notes the reply regarding 
deployment of CAPFs in LWE areas to provide support to the State police forces till the 
situation comes under control. The Committee reiterates its recommendation that the  the 
CAPFs should be deployed to meet the emergency situation/crisis in states and the requests for 
extension of deployment and increase in the quantum must also be examined and linked to the 
development of State police capabilities. 
(Para 3.10.6) 
 
 The Committee notes that the out of 9338 km sanctioned roads under Road Connectivity 
Project for LWE Affected Areas (RCPLWE) only 1796 km length of roads have been 
completed. The Committee would like to know the reasons regarding abysymally slow 
progress in completion of these roads specially with respect to Telangana where 147 km has 
been completed out of 705 km and Chhattisgarh where 319 km has been completed out of 2479 
km. The Committee is of the view that delay in construction of roads in most sensitive LWE 
areas like Telangana and Chhattisgarh is also a reason for slowing down the inclusion and 
development processes of these regions and negatively affecting the capability of CAPFs/ State 
police in tackling the LWE menace. 
(Para 3.10.13) 
 
 
 

 
 
68 
 
Border Infrastructure & Management 
 
 The Committee also recommends that the Ministry should establish an inter-State forum 
of all the international border sharing Sates for interaction between the heads of State Level 
Empowered Committees of different States under the guidance of the Ministry of Home Affairs 
so as to allow them to share the best practices for enhancing their absorption capacity and 
optimize utilization of allocated funds. 
(Para 3.11.3) 
 
 
Schemes for Safety of Women 
 
 The Committee notes that the funds have been allocated for Central Victim 
Compensation Fund (CVCF) Scheme for compensating women victims of acid attacks, rape, 
trafficking, etc. The Committee appreciates the necessity and significance of the CVCF Scheme. 
However, the Committee feels that this Scheme could have been funded from sources other than 
Nirbhaya Fund, which was meant for funding dedicated initiatives aimed at enhancing the safety 
and security for women in the country. The Committee feels that sanctioning funds from 
Nirbhaya Fund for schemes pertaining to compensation would render the entire fund as a fund 
for merely disbursal and would not have a desired impact at the ground level in enhancing the 
security scenario for the women. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the 
Ministry should desist from sanctioning funds for such Schemes from Nirbhaya Fund and 
adhere to the original purpose of Nirbhaya Fund.  The Committee further recommends 
establishment of a State- of- the- art DNA Labs at various places  to strengthen forensic 
investigation across the country.  
(Para 3.12.6) 
 
 
Demand No. 49 - Andaman and Nicobar Islands 
 
 The Committee notes the reply and recommends to expedite the finalization of Techno-
Commercial Bid for commissioning of Tsunami Early Warning Siren System in 35 places in A & 
N Islands by BSNL so that its installation can be done to strengthen the resilience and 
prepardeness of the A&N Islands against disasters. 
(Para 3.13.7) 
 
 The Committee also notes the reply of the UT that due to lack of availibility of quarry 
products and unavoidable administrative reasons,  the UT was not able to fully utilize the funds 
allotted under several heads such as Agriculture  and Allied Activities, Rural Development, 
Medical and Public Health, Social Welfare, Roads and Bridges, Shipping, Housing and Urban 
Development The Committee feels that such underutilization of the developmental projects in 
the UT is inexplicable. Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that necessary measures 
may be taken to achieve full utilization of funds under various heads. The Committee also 
recommends the MHA to ensure that the fund utilization status of A&N Islands be reviewed on a 
monthly basis and corrective measures are taken in proactive manner.  
(Para 3.13.8) 
 
Connectivity of the UT of Andaman & Nicobar Islands with the mainland 
 
 The Committee understands the requirement of air conectivity of the UT of Andaman & 
Nicobar Islands with the mainland and recommends the Ministry to cap the flight fares from the 

 
 
69 
 
Island to the mainland to provide affordable air travel to the Islanders especially to the weaker 
sections. The Committee further recommends to increase number of flights based on demand to 
ensure 24X7 connectivity of the island with the mainland. 
(Para 3.13.12) 
Power 
 
 The Committee appreciates the islands plan to achieve De- dieselization from 9% to 93% 
in next 3 years that will also promote the use of Renewable energy Sources (RES) in the islands. 
The Committee also notes ongoing/completed solar, wind and LNG projects to cater the energy 
demand of the island and further recommends the Ministry of Home Affairs Administration of 
the A&N islands may undertake a feasibility study of the other RES like thermal energy, tidal 
energy, floating find farm, etc. to meet the energy needs of the Islands. 
(Para 3.13.17) 
 
Demand No. 51 - Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 
 
 The Committee notes that the allocation made in BE 2020-21 for UT of Dadra & Nagar 
Haveli and Daman & Diu is less than the projection. The Committee believes that shortage of 
funds will arrest the development of the UT. Therefore, the Committee would like to be apprised 
about the sector-wise projects proposed/ undertaken for the holistic development of the newly 
merged UT so that correct assessement of requirement of funds can be done and accordingly can 
also be enhanced at RE stage and also in the next fiscal year. 
(Para 3.14.3) 
 
Demand No. 54 - Transfers to Delhi 
 
Water Treatment Plant 
 
 The Committee would like to know the reasons as to why the project was required to be 
revalidated. The Committee emphasize that all operational glitches be removed and expects that 
Water Treatment Plant would be operations at the earliest. 
(Para 3.15.3) 
 
Demand No. 55- Transfers to UT of J&K 
 
 The Committee notes the reply of the UT of J&K that they have taken up the matter 
regarding exemption to handloom and handicraft sectors from GST with the GST Council. The 
Committee would like to know about the final decision taken by the GST Council in this matter 
as this is a crucial aspect for promoting the rich handloom and handicraft tradition in the UT of 
Jammu & Kashmir. 
(Para 3.16.3) 
 
 The Committee would like to be apprised about details of the projects undertaken/ 
proposed for creating necessary social and physical infrastructure for attracting new industries 
and entrepreneurs in Jammu and Kashmir. The Commiitte further reiterates its 
recommendation o f  setting up a Planning Board and investment promotion agency in J&K in a 
stipulated time to formulate investment plans and coordinate with the industries from various 
sectors and countries to increase investment in J&K. The Committee also desires to know about 
the details of investment proposals received for the UT of J&K since its creation. 
  
(Para 3.16.7) 

 
 
70 
 
Employment 
 
 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and reiterates its recommendation for 
expediting the assessement and recruitment so as to fill the vacancies in a time bound manner. 
 
(Para 3.16.10) 
Home Guards 
 
 The Committee feels that MHA should continue pursuing remaining thirteen States for 
implementing the Supreme Court's order and implement it in the UTs of Ladakh, J&K and 
Dadra & Nagar Haveli at the earliest. The Committee also recommends that the division 
concerned of MHA may send a monthly reminder on this issue to the remaining States and

(Para 4.1.4) 
 
Delhi Police 
 
 The Committee desires to be apprised about the progress made in the ITMS project in 
Delhi. 
(Para 4.2.3)  
 
Central Police Organizations 
 
 The Committee would like to be apprised about the details of utilization of funds by 
NCRB for year 2019-20 to assess the pattern of spending by NCRB. 
(Para 4.3.4) 
 
Marine Immigration Posts  
 
 The Committee notes the existing infrastructure at Dhubri, Pandu, Silighat and 
Karimganj Ports of Call. The Committee further recommends the Ministry to co-ordinate with 
the Ministry of Shipping and Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) to ensure timely

and initiate the modernization/ upgradation at Pandu and Karimganj Ports of Call on priority

(Para 4.4.7) 
Border Infrastructure & Management 
 
 The Committee notes the reply regarding progress made at Rupaidiha, Sutarkandi & 
Sunauli ICPs and further recommends to expedite the land acquisition and preparation of DPRs

and cost overrun. 
(Para 4.5.5) 
 
 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry regarding installation of Tsunami Early 
Warning Siren System and recommends to finalise the tenders at the earliest and update the 
Committee about the progress in the matter. 
(Para 4.5.8) 
 
 

 
 
71 
 
 
Medical and Public Health 
 
 The Committee takes note of the reply furnished by the Ministry and desires to be 
apprised about the physical and financial progress achieved with respect the construction of 
Medical College in the UT of A&N Islands along with the timeline for completion. 
(Para 4.6.3)

 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry that the amount to the tune of Rs 150 
crore for Vessel Related Charges and Cargo Related Services payable to PMB, Port Blair are

Demand No. 50-Chandigarh 
 
 The Committee desires to be apprised whether the Ministry of Home Affairs was able to

 The Committee considers the present reply as an interim one and desires that it may be

Power 
 
 The Committee considers this as an interim reply and should be informed when the

 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry regarding the decision of conducting a

(Para 4.8.13) 
 
Zirakpur-Tribune Road 
 
 The Committee would like to be updated about the progress made and latest status

(Para 4.8.18)

Tourism 
 
 The Committee would like to be updated about about the completion status of the 
projects mentioned by the Administration of The UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman &

 The Committee notes the reply of the UT of Ladakh and recommends setting up of

(Para 4.10.3) 
 
Demand No. 53 – Lakshadweep 
 
 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and would like to be apprised about the

(Para 4.11.3) 
 
Demand No. 55 - Transfers to Jammu & Kashmir 
 
 The Committee recommends MHA to take up the matter with the Ministry of Civil

 The Committee notes the reply and reiterates its recommendation to fill vacant posts in a

 The Committee notes the present reply and awaits the final decision/comments as

Report 
 
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of 
Development of North Eastern Region on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Twenty 
Fifth Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2020-21) of the Ministry.  The Two Hundred 
Twenty Fifth Report was presented to Rajya Sabha /laid on the Table of Lok Sabha, on 5th March, 2020. 
 
2. Action Taken Notes as received from the Ministry of DoNER in respect of the recommendations 
contained in the Two Hundred Twenty Fifth Report have been categorized as follows: 
 
Chapter I: The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Government: 
Para Nos. 2.2.10, 2.6.4, 3.2.12, 3.5.7, 4.4.9, 6.1.8, 6.6.7, 6.10.7, 6.11.4, 6.15.6 (of  Two Hundred 
Twenty Fifth Report)    
Total recommendations- 10  
 
The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as 
mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report. 
 
Chapter II: The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to 
pursue in view of the Government’s replies: Para Nos. 3.6.7, 4.1.11, 4.3.8, 6.15.4 (ibid)  
Total recommendations - 04 
 
The Committee is convinced with the explanations furnished by the Ministry and, 
therefore, does not want to pursue the recommendations further. 
 
Chapter III: The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee is not 
satisfied with the replies of the Ministry: Para Nos. 2.2.5, 2.7.4, 3.2.14, 5.2.8, 6.3.6, 6.9.4, 6.14.5 
(ibid)  
Total recommendations - 07  
 
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of its 
recommendations contained in Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry should furnish 
convincing action taken steps in respect of those recommendations.  
 
Chapter IV: The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the 
Government have not been received: Para Nos. 3.2.17, 3.3.4, 3.14.4, 4.2.5, 5.1.9, 6.5.9, 6.8.2, 
6.12.11, 6.14.4, 6.16.4 (ibid)  
Total Recommendations - 10  
 
The Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish pointed and detailed Action 
Taken Notes in respect of the observations/recommendations made in all chapters of the 
Report.  
 
3. The details of the ATNs have been analyzed in the succeeding chapters.

Chapter- I 
 
Recommendations/Observations which have been accepted by the Government 
 
 
1.1 Utilisation of Funds during the Last Three Years 
  
Recommendation 
 
1.1.1 The Committee appreciates the role of the Ministry in recommending reallocation of resources 
within the overall pool to the other Ministries and recommends that the Ministry must strengthen the 
aforesaid mechanism for better coordination among the other Ministries/Departments and better 
utilization of funds allocated. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should strengthen 
the project management system and all pending projects should be completed by the Ministry as a 
Special Mission mode drive. 
 (Para 2.2.10 of 225th Report) 
Action Taken  
 
1.1.2 As already informed, Ministry of DoNER regularly monitors and reviews the expenditure of Non 
exempt Ministries/Departments under 10% Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) on a quarterly basis. All 
Non exempt Ministries are advised to regularly monitor the expenditure against 10% GBS for North 
East and if necessary modify existing schemes and formulate NE specific Schemes. The Ministry is also 
empowered to recommend reallocation of likely surrenders of their Statement 11 allocations to those 
Ministries/Departments who have the absorptive capacity to implement additional schemes/programmes 
within the financial year. During the financial year 2019-2020, three review meetings were held on 06 th 
August, 2019, 11 th October, 2019 and 16 th January, 2020 respectively to assess the utilization of the 
10% GBS earmarked for NER and necessary proposal for additional allocations for inclusion in the 
supplementary demands were sent to the Ministry of Finance. This is a step towards minimizing the 
accruals to NLCPR of the unspent balances of 10% GBS at the end of the year. Besides, efforts are also 
made to collect the actual expenditures figures of the non exempted Ministries on a real time basis in 
the PFMS for better monitoring. The proposal of Ministry of DoNER for specific coding of expenditure 
in sanction orders to be issued by non exempt Ministries, as proposed by CGA from the Financial Year 
2020-21, that would ensure real time expenditure figures for NER, thereby greatly helping in 
monitoring and expenditure of earmarked funds was taken up with Secretary, Department of 
Expenditure. The recommendation of Committee on strengthening the project management system and 
completion of all pending projects as a Special Mission mode drive is noted. 
 
Further Recommendation 
 
1.1.3 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.  
 
 
1.2 Revenue Section 
 
Recommendation 
 
1.2.1 The Committee notes that there is a shortfall of Rs. 2165.49 crore in the allocation in BE 2020-
21 vis-à-vis the amounts projected i.e. Rs. 4495.63 crore by the Ministry for its various schemes. The 
shortfall is too steep, particularly under the schemes of the NEC and North East Special Infrastructure 
Development Scheme and will adversely affect the infrastructure development in the North Eastern 

3 
 
Region. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the increased allocation at RE stage in 
2020-21 may be considered by the Ministry of Finance if allocated funds at BE stage are utilized fully. 
 
 (Para 2.6.4 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
1.2.2 The recommendation of the Committee is noted for compliance. The requirement of additional 
funds will be taken up with the Ministry of Finance at the RE stage in FY 2020-21 based on various 
factors like progress in expenditure, reduction of outstanding UCs, Unspent balances, projections and 
demands of the MDoNER etc., and other related considerations. 
 
Further Recommendation 
 
1.2.3 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.  
 
1.3 Schemes of NEC 
 
Recommendation 
 
1.3.1 The Committee appreciates the role of the North Eastern Council (NEC) in formulation of 
regional plans for integrated and balanced socio-economic development of the NER. Therefore, it is 
pertinent that NEC must synchronise the efforts made under central projects/schemes and efforts of the 
State Government of NE regions to achieve the objectives of inclusive growth and equitable distribution 
of benefits of socio-economic development to the lower rungs of the society. The Committee also takes 
note of the efforts made by the NEC to liquidate the huge committed liabilities against ongoing and 
completed projects which depend on receipt of Utilization Certificates from state governments and 
implementing agencies respectively. The Committee recommends that the Ministry must put all its 
efforts for clearing of liabilities of on-going projects and undertake strict measures to resolve the i ssues 
of non-receipt of Utilization Certificates from the state governments for the future projects. 
 
 (Para 3.2.12 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
1.3.2 During the last two years, the NEC has been concentrating primarily on liquidating the 
committed liabilities under "Schemes of NEC" and no major new liability has been created under the 
scheme. Regular reviews with the State Governments/ implementing agencies are being done to stress 
on the need to furnish the utilization certificates on time and complete the projects.  Such efforts will 
continue in the future as well. 
 
Further Recommendation 
 
1.3.3 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.  
 
 
1.4 Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR-state)  
 
Recommendation 
 
1.4.1 The Committee notes that as Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR) Scheme has 
been restructured into a new scheme North East Special Infrastructure Development Scheme (NESIDS) 
w.e.f. 15 th December, 2017 no new projects are being sanctioned under NLCPR-State scheme and Rs. 

4 
 
407.16 crore, allocated in 2020-21 under NLCPR-State scheme, is for meeting the expenditure towards 
the committed liabilities of the ongoing projects. The Committee also notes that the projected demand 
under NLCPR-State was Rs.1000.00 crore. In absence of any clarification furnished by the Ministry, the  
Committee fails to understand whether the projected demand of Rs.1000.00 crore was for meeting the 
committed liabilities or for the implementation of the projects. Therefore, the Committee desires that the 
Ministry may clarify the same and feels that if the projected demand was for meeting the expenditure 
towards the committed liabilities of the ongoing projects, then the Government should make a one-time 
provision towards meeting the committed liability so that the implementation of the projects could be 
carried out without the burden of a large committed liability and the Government must strengthen the 
monitoring mechanism and continuously review the projects that are pending. 
 (Para 3.5.7 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
1.4.2 The projected demand of Rs.1000.00 crore was for releasing the funds against ongoing projects 
only under NLCPR-State scheme. Continuous efforts are being made by the Ministry for timely 
implementation of projects under NLCPR scheme and meeting the committed liabilities in respect of the 
ongoing projects. The ongoing projects under NLCPR schemes are regularly reviewed in the meetings of 
Inter Ministerial Committee (IMC)/North East Special Infrastructure Development Scheme (NESIDS) 
Committee; through video conferencing with the senior officers of the State Government and during 
visits of senior officers of Ministry of DoNER to NE States. During the F.Y. 2019-20, Rs.379.19 crore 
was released in respect of the ongoing projects under NLCPR scheme. With the rigorous exercise of 
review of ongoing projects and continuous follow up with the State Governments, 62 ongoing projects 
costing Rs.841.34 crore were completed in the F.Y. 2019-20. 
  
Further Recommendation 
 
1.4.3 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.  
 
 
1.5 Social and Infrastructure Development Fund (SIDF) 
 
Recommendation 
 
1.5.1 The Committee notes the reasons for delay in utilisation/slow progress of projects but takes 
strong exception to the low utilisation i.e 44.66% in 2018-19 and 26.05 % upto 31 st January, 2020 in 
2019-20 under the Social and Infrastructure Development Fund (SIDF). Therefore, the Committee 
recommends that effort need to be made by the Ministry of DoNER to accelerate the utilisation of funds 
under the SIDF. The Committee  also recommends that M/o DONER must take a lead in coordinating 
with   the State Governments  for formulating infrastructure projects so that all projects are submitted in 
time for final approval and entire allocation is utilized.  
(Para 4.4.9 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
1.5.2 In compliance of the recommendations of the Hon'ble Committee, this Ministry has been 
continuously raising issue of slow utilization of funds with the respective North Eastern State 
Governments during IMC meetings and during visits of Chief Nodal Officers/ Nodal Officers. This has 
resulted in better expenditure position in this Financial Year under SIDF i.e. release of Rs.27.89 crore. 
Out of revised estimates of Rs.40.00 crore under SIDF. The Ministry is making all-out efforts for timely 
submission of documents by the State Government to expedite the release of pending instalments. The 
total expenditure of Ministry, for the Financial Year 2019-20, was more than 99.5% of the revised 
estimates. This has been achieved by putting in place a robust system in which the officials of the 

5 
 
Ministry regularly interact with the State Governments to ensure that the proposals which are sent to 
the Ministry for approval/sanction are properly formulated in respect of the guidelines of the schemes, 
and submitted in time, to ensure that the time taken for approvals is minimised, and the funds allocated 
are utilised timely. 
 
Further Recommendation 
 
1.5.3 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.  
 
 
1.6 Vision 2020 
 
Recommendation 
 
1.6.1 The Committee recommends that specific monitoring mechanism must be put in place to ensure 
timely implementation of projects undertaken under Vision 2020 Document. The Ministry of DoNER 
should expedite the process of implementation of the projects so that the development process in th e 
region is accelerated to achieve the objectives of mission of Vision 2020. The Committee is of the 
considered view that a perceptible change with regard to development of the North-Eastern region needs 
to be felt. Therefore, strict adherence to the timeline within the stipulated cost needs to be ensured while 
executing implementing projects/schemes. 
(Para 6.1.8 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
1.6.2 The Ministry of DoNER in pursuance of achieving the objectives of mission of Vision 2020 is 
implementing projects in infrastructure sectors of road, power, water supply, health and education, etc., 
bridging the gaps in NER. The Ministry is in agreement with the Committee that timely implementation 
of projects under Vision 2020 Document would fulfill its objectives. In that direction, close coordination 
and communication between MDoNER and NE State Governments for project implementation is being 
strengthened. Supervision and due diligence which plays an important factor in the progress of projects 
is also being expedited. The steps taken to strengthen the monitoring mechanism are (i) Online portal 
for specific schemes/projects, (ii) Payment through PFMS, (iii) Geo-tagging of project sites, (iv) 
Monitoring of physical progress through geo tagged photographs, (v) ‗Just in time‘ release of funds 
(linked to physical and financial progress), and (vi) Super-check of progress of projects by Technical 
Wing of the Ministry, on sample basis. North East Space Application Centre, Shillong is actively 
engaged with MDoNER and NEC for project monitoring through satellite imagery, geo-tagging, etc.  
 
1.6.3 NEC in particular, in line with the NER Vision 2020 Document has considered and sanctioned 
project proposals of the State Governments of NER. NEC has a robust system in which all the projects 
are regularly inspected through field inspections by officers of NEC and Regional Level Monitors 
(RLM). In addition, quarterly review meetings are conducted with the State Governments of NER and 
implementing agencies to ensure timely completion of projects as well as to avoid time and cost 
overrun.  These efforts no doubt, would ensure timely completion of projects within the stipulated cost.  
 
Further Recommendation 
 
1.6.4 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.

1.7 Civil Aviation  
 
Recommendation 
  
1.7.1 The Committee hopes that with the completion of ongoing/new projects would smoothen the air 
connectivity and operational efficacy of Civil Aviation in NER. The Committee recommends that these 
ongoing projects be completed in the stipulated time frame and without cost overruns. The Committee 
desires that the Ministry of DoNER should coordinate with the Ministry of Civil Aviation and the State 
Governments concerned and remove the bottlenecks, if any, in implementation of the projects 
undertaken. 
 (Para 6.6.7 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
1.7.2 Ministry of DoNER coordinates with the Ministry of Civil Aviation regarding the status of 
implementation of the ongoing/new projects undertaken by Ministry of Civil Aviation and its 
bottlenecks, if any, on a regular basis that would smoothen the air connectivity and operational efficacy 
of Civil Aviation in NER. While the projects are reviewed by the concerned sectoral Ministry i.e. 
Ministry of Civil Aviation internally, an Inter-Ministerial Committee on Civil Aviation (IMC) was 
constituted in order to fast track the development of infrastructure projects on airports in NER. IMC-
Civil Aviation also envisages for greater synergy in ongoing efforts in development of aviation sector in 
NER and Tourism and review issues involved in implementation of schemes/programmes and their 
convergence. Since the constitution of IMC-Civil Aviation, 5 IMC meetings have been held and the 5 th 
IMC was held on 16 th October, 2019. Besides, the ongoing/new infrastructure projects are also 
monitored at the level of Secretary, Ministry of DoNER through the quarterly review of projects above 
Rs 100 crore. 
 
Further Recommendation 
 
1.7.3 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry. 
 
1.8 Tourism 
 
Recommendation 
 
1.8.1 The Committee takes note of the projects related to tourism promotion that are being 
implemented under the NESIDS Scheme and hopes that with concerted efforts to implement these 
projects, niche and high end tourism will be developed in the NER. The Committee is however, not 
happy to note that the educational tourism has not been explored in an organized manner by NE 
States. The Committee therefore recommends that Ministry must take steps to explore educational 
tourism with an aim to make education more accessible and providing qualified Human Resource for 
Tourism and Allied services for North Eastern Region States. This will help in making North East 
India a preferred destination for visitors and tourists and generate a pool of qualified youth for 
handling tourism activities there. 
(Para 6.10.7 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
1.8.2 The recommendations of the Committee are noted. Further, it is submitted that the objectives 
of NESIDS include filling up gaps in specified sectors of physical infrastructure relating to water 
supply, power and connectivity to enhance tourism. The physical infrastructure which will be created 
with the projects sanctioned under this scheme will play a crucial role in increasing tourist inflow to 
the North Eastern Region. The scope of NESIDS also includes infrastructure projects in the field of 

7 
 
primary and secondary education, and it has always been an endeavour of the Ministry to give due 
importance to projects received in this sector, from the North Eastern States. Due focus would also be 
given to infrastructure projects in the field of primary and secondary education, which promote 
educational tourism, upon receipt of such project proposals from the State Governments. 
 
Further Recommendation 
 
1.8.3 The Committee note the reply of the Ministry and desires to be apprised about the 
progress made in this direction.  
 
 
1.9 North East Industrial Development Scheme (NEIDS) 
 
Recommendation 
 
1.9.1 The Committee is displeased to note that no fund has been sanctioned under NEIDS and 
respective State Level Committees of NEIDS have not recommended release of funds to any 
company. The Committee therefore recommends that a strategy should be chalked out to implement the 
programme/action plan to boost integrated and balanced industrialization in NER and to promote 
employment in the North East States. 
(Para 6.11.4 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
1.9.2 NEIDS 2017 Scheme guidelines require all eligible industrial units to register with Department 
for Promotion of Industry & Internal Trade (DPIIT) through the portal and applicants have to submit 
applications along with DPRs.  As on date, 104 industrial units have been registered by the empowered 
committee based on the recommendations of the State Government. Units should start commercial 
production within 18 months of registration and thereafter file their claims within one year from their 
date of commercial production under Central Capital Investment Incentive for Access to Credit 
(CCIIAC).  After constant follow up and requisite hand holding by District industries Centres, only 67 
claims that were able to start their commercial production could be registered on the web portal for 
processing. 
  
1.9.3 As no claims were received from State Governments, no allocation was initially made in NEIDS 
Scheme for BE 2019-20.  At RE stage, after constant follow-up, State Level Committee (SLC) of Assam 
confirmed about some claims being ready for consideration and a token amount of Rs. 1.00 crore was 
allocated.  Govt. of Assam conducted the first meeting of SLC and considered the claims of six industrial 
units on 17 th March, 2020.  Based on the recommendations of the SLC, Rs.1.00 crore was released as 
advance to the 6 Industrial units in March, 2019 through NEDFi before the mandatory Pre-Audit. In the 
current financial year (2020-21), an allocation of Rs.100 crore has been made and efforts are being 
made to speed up the process of disbursal of incentives, by revisiting and simplifying stages involved in 
processing of the claims. 
  
1.9.4 In order to speed up the processes, all stakeholders are being engaged through symposiums and 
workshops to build up their capacity. A mega Symposium was held on 30 th November, 2019 on 
―Accelerating Investment & Industrial Development in North -Eastern Region‖ with Invest India and 
Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) Divisions of DPIIT. Participants included Heads of Industries 
Departments of all the 8 NER States, APEDA and NER representatives from CII, FINER, ASSOCHAM, 
FICCI, etc., besides manufacturing and services sector units located in North East Region and other 
stakeholders. Regular meetings through Video Conferencing are held with the State Governments to 
ensure that claims are processed and placed before SLCs for approval.    

8 
 
Further Recommendation 
 
1.9.5 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.

1.10.3 As evident from the above table, no doubt, there is disparity among the NE States in different 
SDG indicators. However, despite inter-state variations in NER, except few indicators, in most of the 
indicators NER States are very close to All-India indicators. For example, in case of SGD-1 (no 
poverty), except Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Manipur other States are above All-India average. So 
far as SDG-2 is concerned, all NE States are above All-India average. In SDG 10 (Reduced Inequality) 
and SDG-15 (Life on Land), NE States are front runners. In SDG-6 (Clean Water & Sanitation) and 
SDG-7 (Affordable & Clean Energy), NE States are very close to All India average, though efforts could 
be made to improve further. SDG-8 (Decent Work & Economic Growth) and SDG-9 (Industry, 
Innovation & Infrastructure) in NE States are comparatively lower than All-India average due to the 
obvious reason that the region is predominantly agrarian and there is hardly any industrialization in the 
region. In crucial indicators like SDG-3 (Good Health), SDG-4 (Quality Education) and SDG-5 
(Gender Equality), the States in the NE region is behind All-India average. These indicators need to be 
improved, which requires concerted efforts by the line Departments like Health, Education and Women 
and Child Development of NE State Governments and Central Ministries. In fact, Central Ministries 
through Inter Ministerial Committee (IMC) were requested to make specific intervention to improve 
these indicators in the NE States. 
 
1.10.4 In appreciation of recommendations of the Standing Committee that Ministry must identify their 
efforts and pursue for additional allocations to reduce this wide regional disparity in the NER, it is 
important to inform the Committee that Ministry is working towards extension of the schemes for the 
next five years (15 th Finance Commission period) with enhanced allocation and expanded scope. The 
projected requirement is Rs.50,000 crore for next five years. The Ministry will take up projects in the 
infrastructure sectors of connectivity, water supply, power, tourism promotion, other sectors of 
importance, etc. Ministry will also take up projects in the social sectors of health and education etc. 
Ministry is setting up virtual smart classrooms with remote teaching facility, to begin with, in secondary 
and senior secondary schools in Aspirational Districts of NE States. The scope of the existing pilot 
scheme of Hill Area Development Program (HADP) is proposed to be expanded to include most 
backward hilly districts and all Aspirational Districts of NER. These initiatives will certainly improve 
the SDG indicators in the NE region. 
    
1.10.5 In addition, Hon‘ble Minister DoNER vide his DO letter dated 02 nd July, 2019 and 11 th 
November, 2019 addressed to Hon‘ble Finance Minister and DO letter dated 07 th October, 2019 
addressed to Hon‘ble MoS for Finance and Corporate Affairs requested for leveraging of accumulated 
balance in Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources (NLCPR) fund for holistic development of NER. 
The Ministry had proposed to utilize the accumulated balance in NLCPR for funding various important 
projects of Ministry of DoNER and NEC in critical areas of connectivity, tourism promotion, water 
supply, power, livelihood, health, education etc. Some resources from this pool will also be utilized for 
taking up projects for holistic development of 14 Aspirational districts of NE, and for development of 5 
key sectors viz. Bambo, Tea, Tourism, Pisciculture and Dairy identified by NITI Forum for North East. 
The Ministry also took up the matter with Ministry of Finance for allocating additional resources for 
holistic development of various sectors through various communications. NITI Aayog also vide its DO 
letter dated 21 st January, 2020 in support of Ministry of DoNER endeavour, impressed the Ministry of 
Finance to allocate additional resources from NLCPR pool where there is an accumulated unspent 
amount of more than Rs. 50,000 crore. However, Ministry is intensifying its continuing efforts and 
pursuing with Ministry of Finance for additional allocations to reduce this wide regional disparity in 
the North-Eastern Region.  
  
Further Recommendation 
 
1.10.6 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.

2.1 North East Special Infrastructure Development Scheme (NESIDS) 
 
Recommendation 
 
2.1.1 The Committee notes that the NESIDS is a Central Sector Scheme with financial outlay of Rs. 
1600.00 crore and is dismayed to note that only Rs 532.39 crore have been utilised under this head 
during 2018-19 and 2019-20 as on 31 st January, 2020. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of 
DoNER in consultation with state government should formulate schemes/projects that may be taken up 
under this scheme. The Committee also recommends that all projects undertaken under NESIDS should 
be completed within the stipulated time frame. 
 (Para 3.6.7 of 225th Report) 
Action Taken 
 
2.1.2 All projects costing Rs.1909.96 crore (including saving of Rs.402.47 crore from NLCPR scheme 
carried forward to NESIDS) have been sanctioned against which an amount of Rs.481.26 crore has been 
released. The Ministry of DoNER was also mandated to release Central Assistance of Rs.200.00 crore 
for re-building totally washed away/damaged infrastructure during floods in 2017 in the North Eastern 
Region. Under NESIDS (Natural Calamity), 45 projects have been sanctioned and amount of Rs.197.83 
crore has been released in financial year 2019-20, as per the entitlement to these projects as onetime 
central assistance. The progress is reviewed during the meeting of Inter Ministerial Committee 
(IMC)/North East Special Infrastructure Development Scheme (NESIDS) Committee and time to time 
through VCs, in addition to pursue through correspondence. A Chief Nodal Officer (CNO) of the rank of 
JS and Nodal Officer (NO) of the rank of Director have been appointed state wise for all the States, who 
monitor the progress of all the schemes. Visiting officers also reviews the progress during their visit to 
the State. 
 
 
2.2 Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC) 
 
Recommendation 
 
2.2.1 The Committee takes note of the above cited reasons for delay in utilization/slow progress of 
projects. However, it is dismayed with the fund utilization capacity of the Bodoland Territorial Council 
as the Council is not able to absorb the allocated fund for developmental activities. The Committee 
expresses its displeasure that no funds have been utilized under this head for FYs 2018-19 and 2019-20. 
The Committee recommends that the funds under this head should be utilized not only optimally and 
efficiently but expeditiously too by BTC as the same would lead to socio-economic infrastructure 
development like road & bridges, power, agriculture, art and culture. The Committee, therefore, strongly 
recommends that M/o DoNER must take a lead in coordinating with the State Government of Assam 
and BTC for formulating infrastructure projects so that all proposals of BTC are submitted in time for 
final approval. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry must have appropriate monitoring 
mechanism in place to ensure speedy execution of projects undertaken including release of funds and 
furnishing of UCs so that projects are completed without any time and cost overrun. 
(Para 4.1.11 ibid) 
  

11

available in RE of F.Y. 2019-20, have been utilised. Against the BTC package value of Rs.750.00 crore,

Certificate in respect of 51 projects costing Rs. 570.19 crore have been received from the State

2.4 Environment and Forests  
 
Recommendation 
 
2.4.1 The Committee feels that mere allocation and release of funds would not be effective in 
expanding the forest cover without robust and effective monitoring, and regular evaluation of the Green 
India Mission.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that measures should be taken in various North 
Eastern states to intensify afforestation programmes. The Committee also desires to be apprised about 
the various outcomes achieved in different States of the NER as a result of implementation of Green 
India Mission. 
 (Para 6.15.4 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
2.4.2 National Mission of Green India has comprehensive monitoring framework at four different 
levels i.e. on-ground self-monitoring, field review by an external agency, remote-sensing-based forest 
cover monitoring by the Forest Survey of India, and monitoring of few pilot areas by the implementing 
agencies to assess the impact and efficacy of different old and new practices. 
  
2.4.3 State Governments submit yearly monitoring reports before seeking funds from the Central 
Ministry. The Mission has also constituted monitoring committees for every state to monitor and 
evaluate Green India Mission (GIM). From 2015-16 to 2019-20, Rs. 108.04 crore has been released in 

12 
 
three North-Eastern states namely Manipur, Mizoram and Sikkim to carry out afforestation activities 
over the 29,950.2 ha area in the various identified landscapes. The Mission is in the process of 
expanding its activities in other NER States based on submission of Annual Plans of Operation of the 
states and availability of funds. 
  
2.4.4 The mission has various components like enhancing quality of moderately dense forest cover, 
eco-restoration of degraded open forests, rehabilitation of shifting cultivation areas and restoration of 
abandoned mining area in North-Eastern States.

Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been

3.1 Utilisation of Funds during the Last Three Years 
  
Recommendation 
 
3.1.1 The Committee takes note of the low utilisation of allocation i.e. 44.66 % in 2018-19 and 26.05 
% in 2019-20 (upto 31 st January, 2020) under the Social and Infrastructure Development Fund (SIDF). 
The Committee also notes the utilization of 4.25 % under Dima Hasao Autonomous Territorial Council-
Special Development Package in 2019-20 and that too after enhancing the allocation by Rs.6.11 c rore in 
RE 2019-20 and no utilisation of funds under Bodoland Territorial Council-Special Development 
Package in 2018-19 and 2019-20 (upto 31 st January, 2020). The Committee recommends that strict 
measures should be undertaken by the Ministry to resolve the issues of late receipt of project proposals 
and non-receipt of Utilization Certificates from the State Governments and the Ministry must furnish the 
steps taken to improve the utilisation. 
(Para 2.2.5 of 225th Report) 
Action Taken 
  
3.1.2 A special drive was made to fetch the project proposals and retain to the tune of entire available

3.4.2 Prag Jyoti Textile Park, Darrang, Assam is a project of Ministry of Textiles and was approved 
on 11th September, 2014 under the Scheme for Integrated Textile Park (SITP). The project cost eligible 
for funding under the scheme is Rs. 47.249 crore, out of which an amount of Rs. 40.00 crore (90%) has

3.4.3 Project was supposed to be completed by March, 2018 (3 years from the date of release of 1 st 
instalment of GoI grant). However it has been informed by SPV that as the Park areas has long rainy 
season and the work remains halted for around 5-6 months every year due to which the project could 
not be implemented on time. 
 
3.4.4 Continuous endeavour was made for actively inspecting the project time to time and observe real 
time progress. After submission of documents for 3 rd instalment, Textile Commissioner was asked to 
submit a progress report. As per the report, some discrepancies in the project were noticed viz. variation 
in physical and financial progress. Based upon these shortcomings in the report, a visit from DC (HL) 
was made to verify the facts and following findings were reported:- 
 
(i) Necessary clearances have been obtained. 

16 
 
(ii) Major constraint in progress is climatic condition i.e. rainy season for 5-6 months affect 
pace of work as also the delay in fund releases affects the construction work. 
(iii) Park will now be completed by March, 2021 as per the projection given. 
(iv) Rs. 13.66 crore has been spent on project (28.91%). 
(v) Park will operationalize 50% units by June, 2021 and 100% by March, 2022. 
 
3.4.5 Based upon this report, the project was placed before the Project Approval Committee on 9 th 
September, 2019 for taking review by Secretary (Textiles). However, Special Purpose Vehicle  (SPV) 
was absent in the meeting and therefore, the matter was deferred till next meeting. In the meantime, to 
gauge the real time progress and ground reality, a field visit was again undertaken by the Joint 
Secretary (Infra) and Under Secretary (Infra), MDoNER on 8 th November, 2019 wherein following was 
noted: 
  
(i) Assam being a rain prone state, it rains almost 5/6 months in a year from March to 
September. Hence, working season is less. 
(ii) MoA between the State and the SPV for land sub lease deed to park is expected within 2-3 
months as informed by SPV yet to be notarized. 
(iii) It was also noted that park is facing shortage of funds and thus could not achieve full 
progress of work. 
 
3.4.6 Accordingly, the proposal was again put up in the PAC meeting held in December, 2019 wherein 
SPV committed to operationalize 4-5 units by March, 2020. PAC decided to accord extension upto 
March, 2020 and for the release of Rs. 2 crores to the project. The funds will be spent on construction of 
roads, boundary walls, street lighting etc. and further extension will be considered based upon the 
progress made. Subsequently, Rs. 2.00 crore was released on 18th February, 2020. 
 
3.4.7 Textile Commissioner vide its letter dated 20 th February, 2020 informed Ministry that the 
progress on the project is at standstill since the last visit. Recently, keeping in view the current difficult 
scenario of Covid-19 curtailments, a further extension of 6 months has also been granted to the project 
vide letter dated 1st May, 2020. 
 
3.4.8 As recommended by the Committee, Ministry of DoNER will take up the matter with Ministry of 
Textiles for co-ordinating with implementing agencies and the line Ministries concerned for ensuring 
the speedy execution of undertaken projects at the specified pace.

Jan Shikshan Sansthan Scheme 
 
3.5.4 Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) aims to provide vocational training to non-literates, neo-literates 
as well as school drop-outs in rural regions by identifying skills that have a relevant market in that 
region. The objective of JSS is to uplift this rural population economically by imparting essential skills 
training, thereby enabling local trades to grow and creating new opportunities for the natives of the 
region. 
  
3.5.5 As on date, 248 JSSs are functional throughout the country. With the objective to expand the JSS 
network to each district of the country, MSDE contemplates  to increase the total number of existing 
JSSs from 248 to 728 in a phased manner during the next five years with increase in existing training 
capacity of 4.15 lakhs to 10 lakhs per annum.  There are 11 approved JSSs in North Eastern Region as 
on date. Further the selection of 12 new JSSs in NER region is under process. Ministry has also decided 
to establish JSS in all the left over districts of NER in its further phases of expansion plan. 
  
Apprenticeship Training
 
  
3.5.6 One of the schemes being implemented by MSDE is Apprenticeship Training under ―The 
Apprentices Act, 1961‖ (amended upto 2014). This Act was enacted with the following objectives to 
fully utilize the facilities available in industries for imparting on the job training and thus developing 
skilled manpower for industries: 
  
(i) To   regulate   and promote the   program  of  training  of apprentices in the industry; and 
(ii) To  utilize   the  facilities  available in industry for imparting practical training with  a view  
to  meeting  the  requirements  of  skilled manpower for industry. 
  
3.5.7 As per the Apprentices Act, 1961 it is obligatory on the part of employers/establishments having 
a manpower strength of 30 or more to engage apprentices in a band of 2.5% to 15% of total manpower 
strength of the establishments including contractual staff. 
  
3.5.8 Under this scheme so far, 245 establishments of NE region have registered on 
―apprenticeshipindia.org.in‖ portal and are engaging apprentices. Currently 2437  apprentices are 
undergoing training and around 6333 apprentices were trained during last four FY i.e. FY 16-17 to FY 
19-20. 
  
 Enhancing Skill Development Infrastructure in N.E Region
 
  
3.5.9 The Ministry had launched a scheme namely ―Enhancing Skill Development Infrastructure in 
N.E Region, with the quite similar objective. This Ministry has taken steps understanding that skill 
development and specialized vocational training of the youth in every state is sine qua non to Human 
Resource Development. This Ministry has already identified various dimensions to address the 
comments raised by the committee in regard of Skill development and specialized vocational training of 
youth. 
  
(i) Specialised skill Training:  Under the scheme ―Enhancing skill development 
infrastructure in NER (ESDI)‖   new trades are introduced in the selected ITIs and introduction 
of these new trades must be based on surveys/feedback of these trades. 
(ii) Upgradation of existing Infrastructure: Under ESDI scheme the Ministry has the 
provision of supplementing the deficient infrastructure of the existing government ITI as well as 
upgradation of various components of these ITI. This Ministry has also a scheme upgradation of

Government ITI into model ITI in 4 states (Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Assam) for

(iii) Upgradation of tools and Equipments: Under the ESDI and Model ITI the provisions 
have been laid down for the procurement and upgrading the tool and equipment‘s. This Ministry

(iv) Creating new Infrastructure: Under ESDI Scheme several new ITI are being constructed

Comments of the Department of Agriculture & Farmers‘ Welfare
 
 
4.9.2 During 2019-20 under Mission Organic Value Chain Development  (MOVCDNER), out of total 
budget of Rs. 160 crores, Rs. 104 crores was released. Major amount allocated for SC Component 
could not be released as the SC population is very less in NER. In order to smoothen the implementation 
of the mission, the following strategies are adopted: 
 
(i) Greater autonomy to states: The states can now sanction infrastructure projects below 
Rs. 25 Lakhs through their State Level Executive Committee instead of utilizing the services of 
NEDFi. Four of the eight States i.e. Manipur, Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram have 
already initiated work on sanctioning such projects while others have started identifying projects. 
 
(ii) Minimum Infrastructure guarantee: The states have been advised to ensure that each of 
the Farmers Producer Companies (FPCs) being formed, are facilitated with at least a basic set of 
enabling infrastructure. These could include custom hiring centres, collection centres and 
transport vehicles. This would help the FPCs in operating efficiently. 
 
(iii) Timeliness of infrastructure development: The states have been advised to sanction the 
above mentioned basic set of infrastructures in the first two years of formation of FPCs. This 
would enable the FPCs to achieve the operational feasibility in nascent stages.

(iv) FPC wise value chain development plan: The States have been advised to provide Value 
Chain Development plan for each of their FPCs along with their Annual Action Plans. This would 
allow the states to plan their implementation of the scheme with better clarity.

community and the FPCs through constant trainings and interactions. This has provided 
researchable issues and some innovative solutions to grassroots level problems. The deployment 
of such solutions is expected to be facilitated under the innovative component of the scheme.

INTRODUCTION 
 
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home 
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby present 
this Two Hundred Twenty-eighth Report on Action Taken by Government on the 
Recommendations/Observations Contained in the Two Hundred Twenty Second Report on 'The 
Management of Worsening Traffic Situation in Delhi '. 
 
2. The Two Hundred Twenty Second Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Home Affairs was presented to the Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of the Lok Sabha 
on the 11 th December, 2019.  
 After presentation/laying of the Report, the copies thereof were sent to 
the Ministry of Home Affairs requesting them to furnish Action Taken Notes on the recommendations 
of the Committee contained in the Report. The Ministry furnished the Action Taken Notes on the said 
report to the Committee on 9th March, 2020.
  
 
3. The Committee has noted that the statement on the status of implementation of the 
recommendations contained in the said Report of the Committee has not been laid on the Table of 
Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha in pursuant to the direction of Chairman, Rajya Sabha dated                              
24th September 2004.     
 
4. The Committee considered the draft Two Hundred Twenty-eighth Report and adopted the same 
at its meeting held on 11th September, 2020.

1.4 Rationalization of Buses And Enhancing the Present Fleet of Buses 
 
Recommendation 
 
1.4.1 The Committee notes that the attempt to initiate the process of induction of 385 electric buses 
has failed as no bidder was found meeting the technical benchmarks and the tender process is be ing 
reinitiated. In this connection, the Committee fails to understand as to why the provision for land for 
parking has not been thought out before setting a target of inducting 1000 electric buses. The 
Committee feels that electric buses though may provide an alternative to fossil fuel but also is viewed 
as one of the most difficult sustainable public transport. So, the Committee strongly feels that the 
Govt. should wait for the successful running of the initial phase and then start processes involved in 
induction of remaining 615 buses. 
(Para 4.5.7 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
1.4.2 Transport Department, GNCTD has informed as under: 
 
(i) Hon‟ble Supreme Court of India in the matter of M.C. Mehta versus Union of India 
&Ors in CWP No.13029/1985 vide its order of July 28, 1998 inter-alia directed 
Government of NCT of Delhi to augment the public transport (stage carriage) to 
10,000 buses by April 01, 2001.  The Hon‟ble Delhi High Court vide its order of 
August 23, 2007 (read with order of September 10, 2007) in the matter of Court on its 
own motion (Crl. W.P. No.878/2007) has further directed Government of NCT of 
Delhi to augment the city bus fleet up to 11000 buses by theend of March, 2009to 
ensure that the order of Hon‟ble Supreme Court is given full effect to. The 
Environment Pollution (Prevention & Control) Authority (EPCA) vide its report of 
No.31 has prayed Hon‟ble Supreme Court of India to inter -alia direct Government of 
NCT of Delhi to add another 6000 buses by the end of 2009, so that the city bus fleet 
be augmented up to 16000 buses. Hon‟ble Supreme Court vide its order of February 
01, 2008 has inter-alia sought the response of Government of NCT of Delhi. Pr. 
Secretary – cum - Commissioner (Transport) vide his affidavit has informed the 
Hon‟ble Court that Government is augmenting city bus fleet up to 11000 buses 
through cluster scheme in accordance with the orders of Hon‟ble Delhi High Court. 
The matter is still pending before the Hon‟ble Supreme Court of India for appropriate 
orders on EPCA plea. As such, Government of NCT of Delhi has to immediately 
augment the bus fleet up to 11,000 buses. The bus fleet could not be augmented 
primarily due to paucity of bus depots space.  
(ii) The matter of paucity of land for bus depots was also raised by the Amicus before the 
Hon‟ble Supreme Court in the matter of M.C. Mehta versus Union of India &Ors. (WP 
Civil No.13029/1985). The Hon‟ble Supreme Court vide its order of January 21, 2016 
inter-alia directed EPCA to examine the matter of availability of lands for parking of 
buses and make recommendations t o the Hon‟ble Supreme Court for providing any 
further space for parking of buses.  
(iii) EPCA had meetings with all the stakeholders and finalized its recommendation in its 
meeting held on May 20, 2016. In addition to the land already available with DTC and 
Transport Department for bus depots, EPCA estimated that 134 acres and 341 acres 
additional land is required to augment the city bus fleet up to 11000 & 16000 buses 
respectively. The said assessment of DDA was excluding the Millennium Bus Depot 
complex consisting of 61.69 acres of land. The report was submitted in the month of 
May, 2016 and since then no additional land has been allotted by DDA to Transport 
Department/DTC for bus depots. The Millennium Bus Depot complex having capacity 
1200 buses was constructed by GNCTD during the Commonwealth Games – 2010.

2.9.3 Major findings of the study are as under: 
 
(i) Traffic data analysis indicated that during Odd –Even Scheme, about 30% personal car 
traffic reduced on road. However there was increase of 6.5% in 2 wheeler traffic, 
19.5% in Taxi, 7.5% in Auto and 4.7%% in Buses. 
(ii) The analysis indicates that net impact of traffic reduction on various roads in terms of 
total volumes ranges from 1% to18% as shown below. Highest impact of traffic 
reduction was seen on GT road (-18.1%) followed by Noida Link road (-15.4%). 
(iii) It has been estimated that average increase in the daily Bus ridership during scheme 
was about 2.8 Lakh amounting to about 5.39% increase. Similarly average increase in 
the daily Metro ridership was recorded about 1.7 Lakh amounting to about 3% 
increase in Metro journeys. Overall, total increase in the daily Public Transport (PT) 
ridership was about 4.5 Lakh amounting to 4.2% increase in PT journeys during the 
Odd Even period 
(iv) It is determined that due to reduction in traffic, average speed on road increased 
between 2% and 15% on various major roads in Delhi 
(v) It has been determined that incidences having speed less than 5 kmph reduced from 
13.7% to 12.4% and incidences having speed between 5-10 kmph reduced from 13% 
to 11.3%. On the other hand, incidences having speed more than 30 kmph increased 
from 21.2% to 24.1% showing lesser congestion during odd-even scheme 
implementation. 
(vi) traffic queue length at junctions were substantially lower during odd-even compared to 
normal days.

2.13 General Observations/recommendations 
 
Recommendation 
 
2.13.1 Some of the major issues with the management of the burgeoning traffic in Delhi are shortage 
of adequate road space, land not readily available for at-grade and multi-level car parking, 
inadequate pedestrian pathways & plazas, multi- modal transport mix, huge number of freight vehicles 
and personal vehicles entering and exiting Delhi from the NCR. A holistic traffic management plan has 
not been drawn up due to lack of coordination between a plethora of agencies who are directly and 
indirectly involved. Road spaces in proximity to Metro stations and markets are clogged with a variety  
of pedestrian and vehicular traffic. Traffic management presently is a difficult task with hardly any 
elbow room for planning and execution. Traffic discipline is at a premium with improvement measures 
too slow to keep pace with increase in vehicles and pedestrian population.  Many areas in Delhi have 
large open spaces some owned by the Government and agencies working under it. If some of these 
spaces could be freed up then comparatively low-cost solutions for improvement of intersection 
geometrics, widening of roads & lanes and automatic multi-level car parking & underground car 
parking could be taken up. In the end analysis land would be the key and many public sector 
organisations and institutions may be required to part with the excess land being held by them. There 
may be hurdles in executing such a plan but a beginning should be made based on an objective survey. 
 
(Para  5.3.1 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
2.13.2 The recommendations of the Committee have been circulated to all the stakeholders of HPC for 
further appropriate action. 
 
Further Recommendation 
 
2.13.3 The Committee takes note of the reply of the Ministry. 
 
 
Recommendation

special parking badges, passes should be made for person with special ability so as to have complete 
universal road infrastructure in Delhi and NCR. 
(Para 5.3.3 ibid) 
Action Taken

further appropriate action. 
 
Further Recommendation 
 
2.13.6 The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry.   
 
 
Recommendation

ambulances, police cars, fire engines, etc. get stuck in traffic jam and delayed in reaching their 
destination. It leads to avoidable loss of valuable lives and property. The Committee recommends tha t

3.13 Diversion of non Delhi bound vehicles from entering Delhi  
 
Recommendation 
 
3.13.1 The Committee notes that there is to and fro movement of more than 12 lakh vehicles everyday 
from neighbouring States of Delhi. The Committee observes that less than one fourth of the total 
vehicular movement is attributed to the freight vehicles. The Committee also observes that the volume 
of both personal and freight vehicles is gradually increasing. The Committee is also aware of the fact 
that the addition of vehicles on the Delhi roads consumes not only road spaces but also affect the 
environment i.e. the emission from vehicles exhaust and their noise increases air and noise pollution in 
the area. The Committee is surprised to note that there is no planning to regulate or restrict the 
vehicular movement from the neighbouring States when the roads of the City are already reeling  under 
heavy stress because of traffic congestion and other related issues. Therefore, the Committee 
recommends that there is an urgent need to formulate plan/policy to regulate the entry of the inbound 
traffic and ensure smooth exit of the outbound traffic by diverting the vehicles using Delhi roads only 
for bypassing via peripheral and ring roads. 
 
3.13.2 The Committee recommends restricting entry of freight vehicles to Delhi during peak traffic 
hours and vehicles which need to reach other destinations and passing through the roads of Delhi 
should be strictly diverted to take the peripheral and ring roads instead of entering Delhi. The 
Committee further recommends to categorise roads on the basis of "prohibit, regulate and restrict" to 
regulate the movement of traffic and to prevent congestion of roads within the limits of Delhi. The 
Committee further recommends that the proposal of patrolling of the border area by joint teams of 
Delhi and Haryana traffic police at the Delhi-Haryana border and at Delhi-Uttar Pra desh border by 
Delhi and Uttar Pradesh traffic police should be encouraged for better management of traffic in the se 
areas. 
(Para  4.7.17 ibid) 
Action Taken 
 
3.13.3 Delhi Traffic Police has informed that formulation of plan/policy to regulate the entry of the 
inbound traffic and ensure smooth exit of the outbound traffic by diverting the vehicles using Delhi 
roads only for bypassing via peripheral and ring roads, is the subject matter of GNCT of Delhi. 
However, the Delhi Traffic Police is diverting non-destined goods vehicles from border entry points. 
Additional deployment of traffic staff has also been made at the borders to check and return non-
destined goods vehicles. During the year 2019, a total of 1,75,070 goods vehicles were checked and 
7,543 non-destined goods vehicles were returned from the border by traffic police.  It is an ongoing 
process for which necessary action is undertaken by Delhi Traffic Police. 
 
3.13.4 In addition, plying and idle parking of goods vehicles has been restricted by Transport 
Department, GNCT of Delhi and Delhi Traffic Police on specified roads during specified timings (24 
hours restrictions, day time restrictions and peak hours restrictions) for different categories of goods 
vehicles i.e. Heavy, Medium and Light Goods Vehicles to prevent congestion of roads within the limits 
of Delhi. The restrictions are being implemented on ground by Delhi Traffic Police. During the year 
2019, a total of 71,752 goods vehicles were prosecuted for violation of no entry timings.  Additional 
deployment of traffic police staff is also ensured at major border entry points for ensuring better traffic 
management in the area. 
 
3.13.5 Uttar Pradesh Traffic Police has informed that 8 districts of Uttar Pradesh (Ghaziabad, 
Gautam Budh Nagar, Bulandshahar, Hapur, Meerut, Baghpat, Muzaffarnagar and Shamli) fall in 
NCR region, in which the two districts Ghaziabad and Gautam Budh Nagar are adjacent to the 
National Capital Delhi.  Action taken on the recommendations contained in 222nd Report are as under:
